significance: A Mauryan site in West Champaran with fifteen stupa mounds in three rows and a ten-metre polished sandstone Ashokan pillar crowned by a lion and carrying Brahmi edicts. Excavations by Cunningham, Bloch and Majumdar recovered figurines, pottery and, inside a miniature stupa, a birch-leaf manuscript of Buddhist text.
story: Some hold that the 26 m brick mound is the stupa in which the Buddha's ashes were enshrined.
